checks.note: subscribeCoach/subscribePlayer check assertCanSubscribe on an unlocked read and claim the row only in persistCoachSubscription/persistPlayerSubscription (findBy*IdForUpdate), so two requests can both call createPaidStripeSubscription — each with a fresh sub-create-UUID idempotency key and error_if_incomplete (per the file's own javadoc), charging the first invoice at create time. The loser hits isOtherLiveSubscription → cancelStripeSubscriptionQuietly, which only calls stripeClient.cancelSubscriptionImmediately with no refund/credit (Stripe's immediate cancel doesn't auto-refund by default, and the same method is reused for grace-expiry cancels where refunding would be wrong), so the duplicate first-period charge is kept.

Confirmed from the diff: createPaidStripeSubscription uses a per-attempt "sub-create-" + UUID.randomUUID() idempotency key, assertCanSubscribe passes when the local stripeSubscriptionId is null (the state after a crash before persistCoachSubscription commits), and the isOtherLiveSubscription duplicate-cancel only fires on a different *locally stored* live id — so a retry creates and charges a second Stripe subscription with nothing in this file cancelling the first. The caveat (whether StripeSubscriptionReconciliationScheduler cancels vs. only alerts on orphans) is unresolvable here, but the cancelStripeSubscriptionQuietly comment says "orphan alert", and even an active reconciler would only shorten the double-billing window, not prevent the duplicate creation.

checkPastDueGracePeriod selects on the local PAST_DUE status, so the race window is the full Stripe-payment-to-invoice.paid-webhook lag, not just the phase-1→cancel gap; cancelAtStripeForGrace does no status re-check, and GraceTarget.matches (per its own javadoc) deliberately revokes a row that went ACTIVE as long as stripeSubscriptionId is unchanged — after revoke clears the id, the late invoice.paid finds no row, so the paid customer is cancelled with no recovery.

applyCoachChange/applyPlayerChange phase 1 commits (releasing the row lock) before syncStripePriceForChange calls stripeClient.updateSubscriptionTier, so a concurrent restoreCoachPriceAndVoidDowngrade (or upgrade) that voids the change leaves the applicator setting Stripe to the downgrade price while phase 2 (pendingCoachChange == null) silently skips without reverting it. handleSubscriptionUpdated explicitly never syncs tier from Stripe ("no priceId→tier map") and reconcileMarketplaceTiers is payment→marketplace only, so the drift is uncorrected.

persistCoachTierUpgrade's superseded guard (`!Objects.equals(stripeSubId, sub.getStripeSubscriptionId())` → log + return from a void method) runs after changeCoachTier already charged the proration via updateStripePrice(chargeNow=true), and neither it nor any other path refunds, retries, or cancels that paid invoice — the caller returns success. Caveat checked: the deleted-webhook race (revokeCoachSubscription nulls the id under lock between the Stripe charge and the persist) is the primary interleaving, with a follow-on re-subscribe as a variant; either way the charge is silently dropped. Same applies to persistPlayerTierUpgrade.

reconcileMarketplaceTiers computes effectiveCoachTier from the batch-loaded `sub` (findAll snapshot) and never re-reads the payment row inside the per-item transactionTemplate block — only the marketplace projection is read fresh (findByCoachId), unlike applyCoachChange/checkPastDueGracePeriod which re-read via findByCoachIdForUpdate. A handleInvoicePaid commit between batch load and the item's turn is therefore overwritten: the sweep sees the recovered projection as a mismatch against stale SCOUT and calls syncMarketplaceTier(coachId, "SCOUT"). Sweep interval and effectiveCoachTier's body are outside this diff but don't affect the mechanism.

The gap itself is visible: changeCoachTier's downgrade branch calls updateStripePrice before self.persistCoachTierDowngrade runs in a separate transaction (restoreCoachPriceAndVoidDowngrade mirrors it), and handleSubscriptionUpdated explicitly never derives tier from Stripe price. But the "never reconciled" claim depends on reconcileStripeSubscriptions() / StripeSubscriptionReconciliationScheduler, referenced in reconcileMarketplaceTiers' javadoc and cancelStripeSubscriptionQuietly but not present in the diff, so the verification caveat (no Stripe→payment price-vs-tier comparison) cannot be confirmed from the shown code.

handleInvoicePaid advances the shared lastStripeEventAt via newer() without writing currentPeriodEnd, and isStaleEvent's strict eventCreated.isBefore(lastApplied) then drops a subscription.updated whose created is one second earlier; persistCoach/PlayerTierDowngrade use sub.getCurrentPeriodEnd() as effectiveAt, so the stale period end propagates. Stripe guarantees neither delivery order nor updated.created >= invoice.paid.created (the rollover update typically precedes payment), so the caveat does not close the window; only equal timestamps are safe.

Code mechanics match: PAUSED is excluded from RECOVERABLE_ON_PAYMENT, requireBillingHealthy throws notActive, assertCanSubscribe throws updatePaymentMethod, and no resume path exists. But the finding's own caveat — whether PAUSED is reachable — depends on Stripe account trial/pause settings (and SubscriptionEntitlement.BILLING_HEALTHY_STATUSES, not shown); the in-app subscribe path uses error_if_incomplete with a required payment method, so the trial-pause route may never occur for app-created subscriptions.

matches.note: R10 identifies the grace-sweep gap (only PAST_DUE selected) and the dead-end for PAUSED, but omits UNPAID entirely and describes the consequence as user lockout rather than the Stripe subscription lingering unclosed and raising invoices.
